Pass any such further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in facts and circumstances of the present case._ In the interim, injunct CTUIL from revoking/ taking any coercive steps in form of releasing connectivity in favour of other developers during the pendency of the present Petition - (f) The Petitioner submitted its Notarised Affidavit dated 25.03.2026 and submitted the same to CTUIL. - (j) Further, in view of the Commission’s Order dated 08.12.2025 in Petition No. 14/SM/2025, in case the Petitioner loses its Right of Refusal, in that case the **3.** The Petition was admitted, and notice was issued to the parties to file reply and rejoinder. The Petitioner was directed to submit a copy of the CTUIL communication dated 20.03.2026 mentioned in CTUIL’s letter dated 15.04.2026, vide which the Petitioner’s application was reverted for rectification. The extracts of the RoP for the hearing dated 06.05.2026 are attached as under: _ “Learned counsel for the Petitioner, RSDCL, submitted that the Petitioner is a Renewable Power Park Developer (RPPD) and has developed a 925 MW Nokh Solar Park under the MNRE Scheme, which achieved COD on 18.12.2025. Learned counsel further submitted that the Petitioner had, on 21.2.2026, applied for addition of generation capacity including ESS within the aforesaid 925 MW capacity, however, Respondent, CTUIL, vide letter dated 15.4.2026, closed the said application on the ground that the affidavit had been submitted on a special adhesive stamp instead of non-judicial stamp paper, treating the same as a major deficiency in terms of the list of deficiencies published by CTUIL on 1.11.2024. Learned counsel submitted that no opportunity was afforded to the Petitioner to rectify the defect in the affidavit and, therefore, the present Petition has been filed, inter alia, seeking taking on record of the affidavit filed by the Petitioner or, in the alternative, permission to upload a fresh affidavit, and for a direction that the connectivity in question may not be released to any other developer till the pendency of the present Petition._ _ 2. Considering the submissions of the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission directed as follows:_ _ b) The Respondent to file its reply to the Petition, if any, within three weeks with a copy to the Petitioner, who may file its rejoinder, if any, within a week thereafter._ _ c) The Petitioner to submit a copy of the CTUIL communication dated 20.03.2026 mentioned in CTUIL’s letter dated 15.04.2026, vide which the Petitioner’s application was reverted for rectification._ - (k) The Power to Relax (Regulation 41) and the Power to Remove Difficulty (Regulation 42) are powers exclusively vested in this Commission. CTUIL, as the Nodal Agency, cannot usurp these judicial/ regulatory powers to grant the reliefs sought by the Petitioner. CTUIL has accordingly acted in due compliance with the regulatory framework and, without prejudice to the same, the question of whether the prescribed affidavit format requirement merits relaxation in the facts and circumstances of the present case, so as to permit re-opening of the Application, requires directions from this Commission. _ “The learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed, inter alia, seeking taking on record the affidavit filed by the Petitioner or, in the alternative, permission to upload a fresh affidavit, and for a direction that the connectivity, may not be released to any other developer till the pendency of the present Petition. The learned counsel submitted that the Respondent, CTUIL, vide its letter dated 15.4.2026 closed the connectivity application of the Petitioner due to a major deficiency i.e. non-submission of the connectivity application on a nonjudicial stamp paper. The learned counsel further submitted that pursuant to the direction of the Commission vide Record of Proceedings dated 6.5.2026, the Petitioner has filed its compliance affidavit dated 22.5.2026. The learned counsel also submitted that the Respondent, CTUIL, in _ _ its reply, has not specifically opposed the reliefs sought by the Petitioner and the omission on the part of the Petitioner was inadvertent and occurred due to an oversight. In view of the above, the learned counsel prayed that the present case of the Petitioner is a fit case for the exercise of the Commission’s Powers to Relax and Remove Difficulties._ _ 2. While not specifically opposing the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the learned counsel for the Respondent, CTUIL, submitted that CTUIL has acted in due compliance with the regulatory framework._ _ 3. Considering the submissions of the learned counsel for the Parties, the Commission reserved the matter for order.” _ **7.** We have perused the submissions made by the Petitioner as well as the Respondent, CTUIL. The following issues arise for our consideration: ** Issue No. 1: Whether the instant Petition is a fit case for this Commission to exercise its Power to Relax and Power to Remove Difficulties in terms of the GNA Regulations, 2022?** **10.** The snapshot of Petitioner’s Notarised Affidavit dated 25.03.2026 is as under: **14.** Accordingly, the action of CTUIL in closing the Petitioner’s application on the above ground cannot be faulted. However, the Petitioner has submitted that closure of the application would result in the Petitioner losing its Right of First Refusal (RoFR) and may result in allocation of the released Connectivity to other developers who may have applied for Connectivity along with the Petitioner. **17.** Petition No. 237/MP/2026 stands disposed of in terms of the above. The order has been passed in view of the peculiar facts of the case and shall not be treated as a precedent.
